**HCALMODULE-20261015-SysArch** — reviewed **`7243c84c055a5c2817f7eb86727ca7eade2f21c8`**. Read-only; no files changed or delegation. Recommendation below is a **PROTOTYPE fixture choice**, with no human sign-off or change to LAYOUT001.

Use the agreed **6×6, 36-tile common board**, with **one H2GCROC-class package per board budgeted for 78 powered channels**, and demonstrate two boards sharing one carrier, interface, spreader and cooling assembly. The mechanical geometry proposed by the coordinator is coherent with the following details.

| Part / boundary | Proposed fixture contract |
|---|---|
| Local frame | Right-handed `(x,y,z)`: x across boards, y toward shared service bay, +z from absorber through tiles/electronics toward cooling/back cover. Origin at carrier face centre, front skin starts z=0. |
| Carrier frame | **380×240 mm**, 2 mm perimeter rails. Inside frame: x=±188, y=±118 mm. |
| Tileboards | **184×184 mm** PCBs, centres **(−93,−12)** and **(+93,−12) mm**. This gives 2 mm board separation, 3 mm minimum x clearance to rails, and a 38 mm rear interior service region. |
| Tile field | 6×6 at 30 mm pitch; inherited 29.7 mm scintillator cores and 0.1 mm wrap give **179.9 mm wrapped footprint** and **2.05 mm PCB edge margin**. |
| Shared service bay | y=85–115 mm; PCB ends at y=80, giving 5 mm clearance. One example motherboard is **350×30×1.2 mm**, centre `(0,100,4.3) mm`. |
| Interface and connectors | One 20×20 mm interface package at `(0,100)` using the ASIC contact stack below. Four illustrative **20×12×2 mm** connector envelopes at x=`−120,−40,+40,+120`, y=100, z=5.95 mm fit the bay. Label LV, bias, data, clock/control and declare their material/package assumptions. These are footprints, not selected connector ratings. |
| Cooling | Carrier-owned **Cu plate z=7–10 mm**, inside the frame. Two 2 mm OD tubes along y at e.g. x=±175, **z=8.5 mm**, have 0.5 mm Cu above/below. Subtract their full OD cylinders from Cu; insert disjoint Ti annuli and water cores. |
| Tube boundaries | Cu cut length 236 mm, tube length 240 mm, extending through rail openings to y=±120. Example 2.2×2.2 mm rail ports give 0.1 mm transverse clearance around 2 mm OD tubes. Four named ports are **two parallel through-flow branches**. A supply/return circuit requires an additional header/U-link. |
| Rear closure | If present: insulation **z=10–10.125 mm**, back skin **10.125–10.625 mm**. Thus **10.625 mm total body depth**, rather than silently retaining DES028’s 10.275 mm. This does not select a future full-detector layer pitch. |
| Absorber | Sector owned. Include one separate **30 mm reference patch** only in the isolated fixture; board/carrier inventories own no absorber. Full assembly must omit the fixture patch and place absorber once. |

The proposed common vertical stack is feasible as an explicit geometry fixture:

- Front skin: z=0–0.2 mm.
- Wrapped tile: z=0.4–3.6 mm; scintillator core z=0.5–3.5 mm.
- Recess: z=2.7–3.5 mm, with a matching opening through the back wrap.
- SiPM package: z=2.75–3.55 mm; solder: 3.55–3.7 mm.
- PCB: z=3.7–4.9 mm.
- ASIC bond: 4.9–4.95; package: 4.95–6.45; graphite: 6.45–6.65; Al post: 6.65–7.0 mm.
- For an inherited 0.8 mm LED package: bond 4.9–4.95; LED 4.95–5.75; graphite 5.75–5.95; Al post 5.95–7.0 mm.

Central **20×20 mm ASIC footprints** at each board centre clear the nearest 2×2 mm LED footprints, located at local `(±15,±15) mm`, by **4 mm in each axis**. LED-to-tile optical injection remains unqualified; adding its heat post does not establish an optical calibration path.

The board seam must remain visible: it has **6.1 mm between wrapped tile edges and 6.3 mm between scintillator cores**. Tile-centre spacing across the seam is **36 mm**, although it remains 30 mm within each board. Use board/tile IDs and an explicit position map; do not impose an uninterrupted global 30 mm grid.

**Ownership and service boundaries**

The tileboard owns its tile cores/wraps/recesses, SiPMs, LEDs, PCB constituents, front end, and contact pads/posts. The common carrier owns rails/skins, one shared interface and motherboard, spreader, pipes/coolant, rail ports and carrier-level connectors. The fixture owns its comparison absorber patch and external handoff markers.

This follows DES028’s sector-absorber contract (`docs/design/DES-028-calorimeter-cassettes.md:32–36`) and DES035’s hierarchy/shared-service direction (`DES-035-hcal-realism-and-prototype-plan.md:135–149`). Do **not** call the old `build_hcal` twice: `tools/calorimeter_hardware/model.py:113–125,145–155` would duplicate skins, cooling, rails and interface hardware. The old square-array and channel invariant at lines 80/161 also needs explicit replacement for board-level powered-versus-connected channel accounting.

Each service record should carry both endpoint owners, position/frame, direction, connector/port envelope, material ownership and qualification state. Internal graph edges may terminate only at declared external handoffs. Logical connectivity can be tested in this prototype; collector manifolds, hydraulic closure, seals, pressure drop, electrical pinout, bandwidth and cooling capacity remain separate engineering work.

Maintainability should describe the actual sequence: isolate electrical services, drain/disconnect four cooling ports, remove back cover/common cold plate, separate thermal contacts, and extract individual boards in +z. Board extraction with the cold plate installed is blocked. The fixture should expose this dependency instead of claiming independent hot replacement.

**Material, power and validation invariants**

1. Every material solid has one owner; fixture absorber is excluded from repeated carrier inventories.
2. Cu plate capacity excludes tube OD cuts; Ti annulus and water core are disjoint. PCB copper is subtracted from dielectric thickness, as in existing `model.py:121–125`.
3. Two boards imply **72 connected tiles/SiPMs/LEDs**, two ASIC packages and **156 paid channels**, with unused channels retained in power accounting unless a documented power-down mode applies.
4. Shared interface power occurs once per carrier. LED, monitoring, link and regulator consumption must be included explicitly or named as missing; aggregation must not erase their heat.
5. Under DES028’s old 2 W interface, 90% conversion, 55 V and 2 µA/tile hypotheses, the **conditional** carrier heat is **3.09681 W at 5 mW/paid channel** or **4.83014 W at 15 mW/paid channel**, before any additionally unbudgeted functions. Ideal 5 K water flow is **0.14817/0.23111 g/s**. These are bookkeeping scenarios, not H2GCROC measurements or thermal qualification.
6. Check all 72 IDs/cells, tile recess/wrap fits, all thermal contact faces, tube bore continuity, four port positions and negative-end transforms where applicable.
7. Independent analytic versus native mass/capacity checks must include rotated Cu cuts; reject blocked ports, duplicated absorbers/shared hardware, missing paid-channel heat and incorrect board-seam positions.
8. Native overlaps, local material rays and saved hits establish geometry/readout behaviour. They do not establish collider rate capability, radiation lifetime, optical response or cooling performance.

**Actual checks:** exact-revision `git show` reads of assigned inputs and relevant manifest entries; verified branch/HEAD; independent standard-library corner/spacing arithmetic passed for all 72 wrapped tiles, boards, rails, ASIC/LED footprints and shared bay. The heat/flow arithmetic above was independently evaluated. No native geometry or engineering calculation was run.
